data.name: Idhika
data.gender_notes: Idhika is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Idhika is derived from the Sanskrit root idh, which means 'desire' or 'intention'. In Hindu mythology, the name Idhika is associated with the goddess Saraswati, the deity of knowledge, learning, and creativity. Idhika represents the inner drive and motivation to pursue knowledge and wisdom. The name Idhika carries the meaning “Desire, Intention” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Idhika usually hope their child will grow to embody desire, intention and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Idhika was a famous poet and scholar in the Sangam period of Tamil literature, from approximately 200 BC to 400 AD.
historical_references.context: Idhika is considered one of the 63 Nayanars, a group of early medieval Tamil Saiva saints. He is famously known for his contribution to Tamil poetry, particularly in the Agam literary genre.

historical_references.reference: Idhika is also believed to have been a contemporary of the renowned Tamil poet and philosopher Thiruvalluvar, who lived around 100 BC to 100 AD.
historical_references.context: While there is no definitive evidence, many scholars believe that Idhika and Thiruvalluvar may have interacted or influenced each other's works due to their close temporal proximity.
